summary.one_liner: Authelia is an open-source authentication and authorization server that provides two-factor authentication and single sign-on for applications through a web portal, acting as a companion to reverse proxies.
summary.what_it_does: Authelia works with reverse proxies such as nginx, Traefik, Caddy, Skipper, Envoy, or HAProxy, allowing, denying, or redirecting requests based on access rules. It offers several second factors: FIDO2/WebAuthn security keys (such as YubiKey), time-based one-time passwords for authenticator apps, and mobile push notifications via Duo. It also supports passwordless WebAuthn/Passkeys, password reset through email confirmation, and locking out access after too many failed attempts. Access rules can match on subdomain, user, group, request URI, method, and network, with one-factor or two-factor policy per rule. The README also lists OpenID Connect 1.0 / OAuth 2.0 support and Kubernetes ingress controller compatibility, and says it can be run highly available with a remote database and Redis.
use_cases: add two-factor login in front of self-hosted web apps
single sign-on for multiple services behind a reverse proxy
protect Traefik or Caddy routes with forward auth
enforce per-route access rules by user or group
passwordless login with passkeys or security keys
OpenID Connect identity provider for applications
how_to_run: See the Get Started Guide in the project documentation
Try the docker compose Local bundle (self-signed certificates, intended for hosts not exposed to the internet)
Try the docker compose Lite bundle (for internet-exposed servers, Let's Encrypt certificates, SQLite and file-based users)
Install as a standalone service from AUR, APT, or FreeBSD Ports, or use a static binary or .deb package
Deploy as a container on Docker or Kubernetes, or via the beta Helm Chart
notable: OpenID Certified for Basic, Implicit, Hybrid, Form Post, and Config OP profiles, per the README
Post-quantum cryptography listed as a feature
Forward-auth integration with Traefik, Caddy, and SWAG from LinuxServer
Supports Kubernetes ingress controllers including ingress-nginx, Traefik, Istio, and Envoy Gateway
caveats: Still under active development, so breaking changes occur; the README recommends pinning a version tag rather than latest
The Lite compose setup does not scale well; high availability requires a remote database and Redis
Docker compose bundles use self-signed certificates and need customization before real use
Sponsors are sought for a security audit; the README says no audit or bug bounty has been funded yet
